current.text: He is projected to start at guard next to Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James and Joel Embiid.
If the starting lineup does not fit, he is the starter most likely to move to the bench.
Philadelphia added Jaylen Brown and LeBron James and has a healthier Joel Embiid, so the ball is shared among several high-usage stars.
Experts expect his usage to drop, likely below 20% and around 18%, because of the usage squeeze in Philadelphia.
Nick Nurse should still give him about 34 minutes a night, which keeps his steals useful.
Experts expect him to fall short of last season's top 70 finish. One sees him ending up around 110th, another says he will drop but not as far as his ESPN ADP of 112.
Experts call his Yahoo ADP in the 60s and a 13 USD auction price too high. They prefer him around picks 80 to 105, and the newest call puts his auction value around 10 USD.
Philadelphia is projected to win about 51 to 52 games. The same preview expects growing pains in October and November and load management for the stars.
The 76ers have 13 back-to-backs this season, three of them in the fantasy playoffs.

durable.text: Steals are his best category, and he rebounds well for a guard.
FG% is his weakest category. He shoots about 44% on 13 to 14 attempts, a mild drag.
His rookie season beat expectations. He came in with an ADP of 97, finished 62nd in category leagues and was top 50 late in the season.
Nick Nurse gives his starters, and his guards in particular, very heavy minutes. He also mixes and staggers lineups when things do not fit.

note: Experts price Edgecombe around 10 USD in our auction, which matches his Yahoo value of 10 USD. Average costs are lower (6.9 USD on Yahoo, 3.8 USD on ESPN), so a bid of 7 to 10 USD is fair, but do not chase him at his Yahoo ADP in the 60s. He has no weak category, his steals are a plus and he rebounds well for a guard. Early in the season, check that he keeps his starting job, gets about 34 minutes and how his usage changes when Embiid or LeBron James sit.
